beats.say: We want to solve E to the power seven point five K equals two. Why take L N, rather than log base ten.
Both logs bring the power down. With log base ten, we get seven point five K, times log E, equals log two.
asks: Why does the power come down?

beats.say: But log E is an awkward number, about zero point four three four. It stays in the working.

do.on: log E is an awkward number

beats.say: L N is log base E. With L N, we get seven point five K, times L N E, equals L N two.
And L N E is exactly one, because E to the power one is E.
asks: Why is L N E equal to 1?

beats.say: So the L N E simply leaves the working: seven point five K equals L N two.
asks: Do both ways give the same K?

beats.say: Both ways give the same K. L N is just neater, because L N E is one.
asks: When do I use log base ten?
